title: fix(update): report when repair leaves an already stopped Gateway offline
body:
Supersedes #153409 (merged onto current main; author @RomneyDa)
Refs #153401

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `update repair` completing without explaining that an already stopped managed Gateway remains offline, while omitting maintenance warnings from its final JSON outcome.

## User Impact

Standalone repair reports the intentional non-start and names `openclaw gateway start`, including the selected profile. Maintenance warnings appear in `postUpdate.doctor.warnings`, with `status: "warning"` and a successful exit when other work succeeds. Installation-drift remediation retains precedence over ordinary start guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor maintenance already owns the service decision and its warning list. Finalization now collects those warnings after maintenance finishes. The Gateway stays stopped unless repair itself owns restoration; parent-owned activation remains with the updater.

RomneyDa's original commit is retained as a merge parent. This changes reporting only: no schema, persisted format, configuration option, or activation policy changes. It applies when the installed candidate runs repair/finalization; it cannot patch an older updater already running in memory. The original PR's published-2026.9.4 recovery-boundary trace remains historical compatibility evidence, not a new native smoke run.

## Evidence

- Full importer and sibling batch on the rebased head with `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1`: **35 files, 1,231 tests passed**, exit 0, **563.2 s**. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m395vb6qjp1wa54b3trdc6zs` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35971076381)); source SHA and file hashes were verified before execution. The lease completed and was stopped.
- Focused proof: **119 tests passed** across `doctor-maintenance.settlement.test.ts`, `update-command-lifecycle.test.ts`, and `doctor-maintenance.installation.test.ts`. Measured single-file `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall times were **13.06 s**, **22.51 s**, and **51.27 s**, respectively. The two new tests took 2 ms and 102 ms in those runs. All three files also passed in the final importer batch.
- **Offline-reporting negative control:** `reports an already stopped Gateway without starting it after repair` fails with an empty warning list when the offline-warning block is removed. The candidate asserts both recorded and logged guidance, with no restart or health call.
- **Finalization-JSON negative control:** `includes service restoration warnings in the repair outcome` fails when warning forwarding after `finish()` is removed: JSON incorrectly reports `ok` and omits Doctor warnings.
- **Installation-drift negative control:** `Doctor handles two-prefix drift through maintenance finish (already-stopped)` fails when the drift branch's early return is removed: ordinary start advice appears alongside the specific installation-repair warning.
- `pnpm check:changed`: **exit 0 in 1,617.7 s**, including core types, all 25 selected test-type graphs, and changed-file lint with zero warnings/errors. This run preceded the single merge-preserving rebase; all five changed files are byte-identical afterward. `git diff --check` also passes.
- Fresh `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean** on the rebased branch. Service operations in the regression proof use synthetic boundaries.
- Known existing test cost: `update-cli.test.ts` passed all 515 cases in **249.644 s** in the final batch (234.146 s in the earlier run). Its split into 22 files is tracked by #157018; that split was not merged into this base. No timeouts, assertions, retries, or test tiers were changed.

Diff size: production **+13/−0**, tests **+36/−0**, documentation **+7/−0**. Hosted PR CI timings are pending at author handoff.
